Went to go check on the animals before I made breakfast this morning, and our bunny died sometime over the night. Poor little guy was curled around his food dish. He was fine when I was prepping some food last night around 2:00 AM. He was only a few months old, and really rather friendly. Other rabbits I've been around throughout the years weren't nearly as friendly as this little guy. My wife was devastated, because she took him in from someone who didn't want him because he was a gag gift anyway, and he became a therapy animal for autistic kids at her school. The kids loved him, and he was a great little dude, but now she has to break it to a bunch of autistic kids that he passed away. I was pretty attached to him too.

It's just one of those things where it's strange to imagine not going up to the cage and having him run up to the door ready to hop into your arms tomorrow morning. I just feel helpless and confused when these things happen. We had a bearded dragon die from agamid adenovirus a few years ago, and there was not one single thing me or anyone else could have done about it, but I still felt tiny and weak because I couldn't save this animals life.

He could have been sick when we got him. He could have gotten an intestinal impaction. No way to know without a necropsy, which we did not do, and just buried him down by the lake. It's hard for me to see my wife in the state she was in, and not have any way to just make things better. It adds to the feeling of helplessness. She's a very emotional person, and trying to absorb that while controlling my own is stressful at times. I also can't help but think "What could I have done to prevent this?", or "Could I have visited with him one last time?". I could have stopped prepping food last night and went to visit with him when I heard him playing around and drinking from his water bottle. It's hard not to think that way, even though logically, I know he was just a baby bunny and as such, a very delicate creature. I can't say I've got too much in the way of empathy for humans, but I do have immense amounts for animals.
